newsitem.title: CHINA: China soybean output to hit 12.17 mln T - report.
newsitem.headline: China soybean output to hit 12.17 mln T - report.

text.p: China's soybean output is forecast to hit 12.17 million tonnes in 1996 and to total 16.79 million tonnes in the year 2000, said an industry report seen in Beijing on Tuesday.

Production of soybeans was expected to rise to 13.93 million tonnes in 1997, 16.82 million tonnes in 1998 and peak at 17.49 million tonnes in 1999, said a joint report by the American Soybean Association and the United Soybean Board.

Increases in soybean production would have to come from yield improvement rather than acreage expansion as China was more eager to develop higher-yield crops such as wheat, corn and rice, the report said.
"The largest constraint on soybean production is the constant competition for land with grain crops," the report said.
Quality problems with Chinese soybeans and a continuing supply shortage meant there was a possibility of largescale imports to China, the report said without elaborating.
China had imported 290,000 tonnes of soybeans in 1995 while exports were 375,000 tonnes, it said. It did not give figures for 1996.
China's total output of oilseeds would hit 38.87 million tonnes in 1996 and was forecast growing to 47.66 million tonnes in the year 2000, the report said.
Oilseeds include soybean, rapeseed, groundnut, sunseed and cottonseed.
China's oilseed output figures do not include soybeans, which is officially classified as a grain.
Population growth and rising living standards would continue to fuel China's long-term oilseed production over the next few years, it said.
